description: Add three new attack modules: HTTP/2 Request Smuggling (modules/h2_smuggling.py), Web Cache Poisoning (modules/cache_poisoning.py), and API Abuse/Rate Limit Bypass (modules/api_abuse.py). Each follows BaseModule pattern from modules/base.py, uses _emit_signal for findings, and includes comprehensive payloads in config.py.
steps: Create modules/h2_smuggling.py - HTTP/2 request smuggling scanner that tests H2.CL and H2.TE desync, CRLF in pseudo-headers, request splitting via HTTP/2 CONTINUATION frames, and websocket upgrade smuggling. Follow the raw-socket pattern from modules/request_smuggling.py. Class: H2SmugglingModule(BaseModule) with name='HTTP/2 Smuggling', vuln_type='h2_smuggling'. Implement test() and test_url() methods. Use _emit_signal for findings with severity CRITICAL, CVSS 9.1+.

Create modules/cache_poisoning.py - Web cache poisoning scanner that tests: unkeyed headers (X-Forwarded-Host, X-Original-URL, X-Rewrite-URL), unkeyed query parameters, fat GET body parameters, cache key normalization issues, host header poisoning, port-based poisoning. Class: CachePoisoningModule(BaseModule) with name='Cache Poisoning', vuln_type='cache_poisoning'. Compare responses with and without cache-busting params to detect caching. Detect cache hits via Age, X-Cache, CF-Cache-Status headers.

Create modules/api_abuse.py - API abuse and rate limit bypass scanner that tests: rate limit bypass via X-Forwarded-For rotation, API key enumeration, GraphQL query complexity abuse (deeply nested queries), mass assignment via extra JSON fields, BOLA/BFLA via method switching (GET->PUT->DELETE), broken function level auth by testing admin endpoints. Class: APIAbuseModule(BaseModule) with name='API Abuse', vuln_type='api_abuse'.

Add payloads to config.py Payloads class: H2_SMUGGLING_PAYLOADS (list of H2 pseudo-header injection strings), CACHE_POISONING_HEADERS (list of unkeyed header names to test), API_ABUSE_RATE_LIMIT_HEADERS (list of IP spoofing headers like X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, etc.).

Register all three modules in core/engine.py _load_modules() dict following existing pattern: 'h2_smuggling': ('modules.h2_smuggling', 'H2SmugglingModule'), 'cache_poisoning': ('modules.cache_poisoning', 'CachePoisoningModule'), 'api_abuse': ('modules.api_abuse', 'APIAbuseModule').
Add CLI flags in main.py: --h2-smuggling, --cache-poison, --api-abuse with action='store_true' and appropriate help text. Add to the modules dict mapping.

Create tests/test_h2_smuggling_module.py with at least 10 test cases: test init, test name/vuln_type, test H2.CL detection with mocked response, test H2.TE detection, test CRLF in pseudo-headers, test no false positive on normal response, test timeout handling, test finding structure.

Create tests/test_cache_poisoning_module.py with at least 10 test cases: test init, test unkeyed header detection, test cache hit detection from headers, test no false positive when no cache, test various header poisoning, test finding structure.

Create tests/test_api_abuse_module.py with at least 10 test cases: test init, test rate limit bypass detection, test BOLA detection, test mass assignment detection, test no false positive, test finding structure.
acceptance_criteria: All three module files pass python -m py_compile without errors
All three module classes properly inherit from BaseModule and implement test() and test_url()
All test files pass pytest execution without requiring external dependencies
config.py Payloads class has new payload lists
main.py has new CLI flags properly connected
mypy --ignore-missing-imports passes on the new module files
verification: python -m py_compile modules/h2_smuggling.py && python -m py_compile modules/cache_poisoning.py && python -m py_compile modules/api_abuse.py
python -m py_compile config.py && python -m py_compile main.py
findings: All 63 tests pass. py_compile passes for all files. ruff linter passes. mypy cannot run due to directory name (Scanner- is not valid Python package name) but AST parsing validates all files. The project uses _emit_signal for findings in all three new modules.
